_comment: GENERATED PIN — the vendored Core schemas' exact bytes, and the contract they came from. Checked by `pnpm check:core-schema` against the platform's DEFAULT BRANCH HEAD, not against `commit` (ui#69): reading the pinned ref made this a tamper check that could not see the platform move, which is the only thing a drift guard is for — the sibling `inspectors/.../platform-pin.json` had already reasoned this out. `commit` is kept as the provenance record of where these bytes were copied from; it is no longer what they are compared against. `core_schema_digest` is Core's SCHEMA_DIGEST at that commit — the contract identity a Bench run pins (VERSIONING.md §4.1), recorded so a drift failure can name the contract rather than only a file. It is reported, not asserted: the digest also covers the platform's .proto sources, which are not vendored here, so failing on it would redden this lane for changes this package does not contain. `frames/generated/units.ts` is generated FROM these bytes by `pnpm codegen:units`; never hand-edit either. To re-sync: copy the files from the platform at its current HEAD, update `commit`, the sha256s and `core_schema_digest`, then re-run `pnpm codegen:units`. See conventions.md §3.1 (cross-language and vendored consumers).
